1.35.betting_forecast: 2/1 Andaman Fifty, 3/1 Jackie Jump Up, 100/30 Baiana, 13/2 Aughlish, Glen And Tonic, 20/1 Enchanted Lady, 50/1 Star Reign,
1.35.spotlight_verdict: The likes of Aughlish and Glen And Tonic look pretty exposed and opposable. Little separated Baiana and Jackie Jump Up at Navan, perhaps the latter can come out on top here, but preference is for Paddy Towmey's newcomer ANDAMAN FIFTY. [Alan Hewison]

horses.spotlight_comment: Palace Pier filly cost 90,000euros as a yearling; half-sister to Listed-placed 1m 2yo winner Defiance (RPR 105); dam placed 7f/1m (76), half-sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Magic Artist, out of half-sister to St Leger and Italian Derby winner Mastery; top yard, newcomer demands plenty of respect.

Useful level of form on latest two of three AW starts, showing plenty of pace when close third over 6f and looked in need of a return to this trip when staying-on second to a clear winner over 5f 10 days ago (from a wide draw); cheekpieces now fitted, and likely more required here on turf debut.
horses.breeding: ch f Soldier's Call - Ty Rock Brandy

horses.spotlight_comment: First foal; 100,000euros yearling; dam unraced half-sister to useful German 6f-7f winner Blueridge Silver, out of South African 1m Grade 1 winner; much improved on second outing last October, speed throughout when beaten 0.5l in Navan auction maiden over this trip (Jackie Jump Up a tenderly-ridden neck away third); can go well if handling better ground.
New Bay filly was a E38,000 yearling; half-sister to 1m4f winner Cycladic (RPR 99); dam 1m2f/1m4f winner (101); always behind after slow start on recent Limerick debut; best watched for now.
Busy 2yo campaign, placed a couple of times on Dundalk AW; at least as good form on last month's seasonal return at the Curragh when beaten under 5l on soft; more needed to play a major role here.

Much the better of three late-season 2yo outings on final occasion when strong-finishing third (neck off runner-up Baiana) in Navan auction maiden in first-time hood, prompting running and riding enquiry; yard have begun the season in fine form, should go well.
Plum last on both 2yo starts and easily passed over on seasonal return.
Some promise in 5f turf maidens for Gordon Elliot at the outset of her career; well held in both handicaps this term, and hard to see her having an impact back in maiden company.

2.10.betting_forecast: 2/1 County Carlow, 100/30 Fate's Gambit, 7/2 Keogie, 9/2 Gia Mor, 13/2 Substance, 16/1 In The Gloaming, 66/1 Basilano,
2.10.spotlight_verdict: Several with similar sorts of chances, notably County Carlow, Fate's Gambit and Keogie, but perhaps it's worth taking a chance on the reappearing GIA MOR, who showed promise in much better-class maidens in the first half of last season on similar ground. [Alan Hewison]

horses.spotlight_comment: Well-beaten last in maidens at the Curragh and Dundalk.
Very lightly-raced 4yo has shown nothing in three starts.

170,000gns yearling; favourite, plenty green when runner-up on debut in Dundalk maiden in late March (7f), following month at same venue forced pace (unbalanced 2f out) but didn't get home over a mile; cheekpieces now fitted and marked drop in trip.

Went close on debut at Dundalk (7f) in January but hasn't reproduced that level of form in three runs since, not getting home on soft/heavy the last twice at the Curragh and Cork; return to better ground should suit and this doesn't look a strong maiden.

Two juvenile runs came in good-quality maidens in first half of season on good ground, not discredited at both the Curragh and Cork; this looks a much weaker maiden so could be interesting if forward enough.

33,000euros yearling; half-brother to two winners (5f to 6f, inc Group-placed); last of 12 on debut at the Curragh in September and forced much of pace on seasonal return before fading on soft ground at Gowran last month; probably more one for handicaps in due course.

21,000euros yearling; half-brother to Czech 7f 2yo/1m3f winner Riwetta; promising Curragh debut in March when staying-on second (4.5l ahead of third-placed Fate's Gambit) over this trip (heavy); didn't get home over a mile under forcing tactics at Gowran last month; return to this trip to suit, and could go well if handling better ground.
Galileo Gold gelding; unraced dam closely related to US 1m Grade 2 winner Ryehill Dreamer; yard not known for Flat maiden winners; watch.

Half-brother to useful 6f/7f winners Ejtilaab and Eqtiraan (Listed); okay Curragh debut last summer behind a stablemate but didn't improve as expected at Listowel, finding stamina test (1m, heavy) beyond him; back in trip for seasonal return and don't rule out.

2.45.betting_forecast: 100/30 Gegenpressing, 9/2 Happy Henry, 5/1 Polar Bear, 6/1 Ukiyo, 9/1 Skillman Ave, 12/1 Rattletheonionbag, 14/1 El Fontenaro,
2.45.spotlight_verdict: The Hartys would love if Sligo had more than just two Flat meetings a year as GEGENPRESSING is unbeaten here and can make it three on the bounce in this race after a pleasing return at Navan. He can turn around Navan form with Ukiyo, who might be best on straight tracks, and Happy Henry who travels well but finds little off the bridle. Navan fourth Polar Bear has stall one, but can miss the break. Two that attracted market support last time, Skillman Avenue and Carrickfinn, aren't without hope. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Half-sister to yard's 5f winner Nouvel Espoir, but she hasn't anything yet in four starts.

Unbeaten in three runs at Sligo and going for three-in-a-row in this race, the last two coming from stall 16; Hayes is elsewhere today, but quite the substitute to have in the saddle and his comeback run was fine.

Strong-travelling maiden went close in 19-runner handicap over 6f at Navan in the autumn, and returned with good effort there in March when just behind Ukiyo (and in front of Polar Bear and Gegenpressing); again found little when let down at Bellewstown latest and head carriage not endearing; might prefer it softer too.
horses.breeding: b g Bungle Inthejungle - Social Butterfly

horses.spotlight_comment: Back with yard after a spell in Britain; yet to place in eight starts and no real progression on AW over the winter; just second run on turf here.

Hasn't won for three years and only had two outings last term; fair fourth in race featuring several of these at Navan (6f) in March and kept on well from long way back (missed break) when third over 5f there last weekend; likely to be strong at the finish, but the break will be crucial from gate one.
horses.breeding: b g Kodi Bear - Blue Marmalade

horses.spotlight_comment: Lots of placed form on AW at Dundalk, including when beaten only half-a-length last month, but still a maiden and her turf form isn't as good.

Smart handicapper back in the day for Eddie Lynam; wasn't able to add to his tally of five wins when moving to Britain; operating at much lower level nowadays, but not showing much for present trainer who tries blinkers here.
horses.breeding: b g Starspangledbanner - Good To Follow

horses.spotlight_comment: Modest performer was third in a couple of 5f maidens last year after finishing fourth (led) over C&D in August; well held in two AW runs in early 2026.
horses.breeding: b f Sea The Stars - Nurse Barbara

horses.spotlight_comment: Won over 6f at Cork on yielding for Gavin Cromwell last year and had several of these behind when quietly-fancied second at Navan in March; decent chance if she's as good around a turning track.

3.22.betting_forecast: 100/30 You Make Me Smile, 4/1 Cornmarket, 7/1 Maxwell Smart, 10/1 Circus Act, Desert Friend, 12/1 Autocrat, Hobart, 16/1 Just
3.22.spotlight_verdict: A big improver over hurdles at this track last year, Cornmarket could be on a good mark for his Flat handicap debut but YOU MAKE ME SMILE (nap) has been coming to hand nicely and is chosen to go back-to-back in this race. She has won before in this reapplied headgear and a top apprentice takes the mount. Maxwell Smart is unlikely to be far away and last year's fourth Circus Act has place claims. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: With the exception of a decent effort on debut, her maiden form has been moderate; not seen since a couple of spins over hurdles last August; tongue-tie on for handicap debut.

Second runner for James Nash; dual-purpose mare has won twice over hurdles; maiden in this sphere but her fourth to You Make Me Smile in last year's renewal was one of her best Flat runs and she has a nice pull at the weights; place chance.

Mayo contender was a revelation for his new trainer last year; won three hurdles on decent ground here, latest over 3m1f; showed nothing in Flat maidens as a youngster, but he's a different model nowadays and could be very well in; has won off similar layoff.

Veteran has done a bit of everything and recorded his eighth win when scoring over 2m on AW in March; poor run at Bellewstown last time but that was only a day after being placed at Dundalk; goes well at Ballinrobe and this track isn't dissimilar.
Best form over 7f/1m, including sole win in Britain as 3yo; stable debut after layoff and not bred for this sort of test.
horses.breeding: br g Dandy Man - Mollie's Girl

horses.spotlight_comment: Old boy has won 12 races in all under both codes, mostly from the front; C&D winner in 2024 and was placed over 1m4f last year, but he's pushing on now and tailed off over fences last time.

Modest dual-purpose performer has done little Flat racing of late; returned from nearly two years off in October and ran well when fourth in long-distance chase last month, but easy to look elsewhere.

Decent performer over this kind of trip; had four seconds (three for this rider) and a win last year and he's had a spin over hurdles to warm up; ground doesn't matter to him and should be thereabouts.
Second reserve; nothing so far Flat or hurdles, but trainer always respected and homebred has staying pedigree (dam won over 2m); handicap debut.

Donegal yard likes to pick up horses with back-form, often from Britain, and try to rejuvenate them; six-time winner at up to 2m but hasn't been finishing out his races in Ireland and been off a while.
horses.breeding: b g Galileo - Laugh Out Loud

horses.spotlight_comment: Got a win on the board over 1m6f at Navan in August but well held afterwards, and is probably going to need this first run of the year.
horses.breeding: b m Raven's Pass - Grand Treasure

horses.spotlight_comment: Locally-owned mare took a long time to come to hand but thrived under both codes last year, recording four wins including this race and a handicap hurdle here in October; promising run at Navan lately and headgear worn for latest Flat win is back on; crack apprentice on board too, so loads to like.
horses.breeding: b m Elusive Pimpernel - Just One Smile

3.58.betting_forecast: 5/2 Yulia, 4/1 Narlita, 11/2 Lady Mairen, 8/1 So Must I, 10/1 Beauparc, Inthesmallhours, 11/1 Chica Guerrera, 12/1 Thrifty Of
3.58.spotlight_verdict: Joseph O'Brien always puts a nice one by for this race, and French import YULIA can give him a third straight win in it. Her form is all over farther, but connections know what they have and must think she'll be fine back in trip around here. You wouldn't readily dismiss stablemate So Must I either, even from out of the handicap. Narlita comes here in great heart but doesn't win that often, while Lady Mairen is better than she showed on her recent return from a layoff. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Won over 1m4f either side of being well beaten in this race last year, and been in good form over that trip on AW lately; dropping back in trip not a positive.
horses.breeding: b m Free Eagle - Secret Path

horses.spotlight_comment: Versatile as regards trip; 1m4f winner last year and finished the season well with placed efforts in big fields at the Curragh, latterly over 1m; too keen on last month's return; would prefer it softer.
horses.breeding: b f Saxon Warrior - Elusive Gold

horses.spotlight_comment: Been busy this year and was fit from AW when winning over 1m at the Curragh in March; touched off on her return there before disappointing when favourite at Gowran; fourth over this trip on AW last time after making the running, and not sure she wants to go this far.

Twice second for this yard after being acquired from a claimer last summer, including a near-miss over 1m at the Curragh in October; never involved on her comeback there over 7f; up in grade and was well beaten in this two years ago; headgear.
Easy winner of 1m4f AW maiden just before Christmas 2024, but not seen since; could be on a fair mark and trainer does well here, but stiff task all the same on turf/handicap debut.
horses.breeding: b m Muhaarar - Not After Hours

horses.spotlight_comment: Respected connections and had smart form at two, placed twice and beaten less than 5l in Curragh Group 3; missed 3yo campaign; disappointing in a winnable maiden on her return over 1m3f at Bellewstown, but trainer has said his horses have been a bit behind schedule this year; handicap debut.

Sole 3yo is second runner for yard with good record in this race; got the better of better-fancied stablemate in AW rated race in February; fair run against male rivals when beaten 5l in strong 3yo handicap at Leopardstown, but she's now 3lb higher as she's out of the handicap; cheekpieces.
Two wins last year, including over just short of this trip at Roscommon on third run of the season; fitter for return and 7lb claimed now; might be capable of more improvement this term.

Trainer has won three of the last five renewals, all with imports making seasonal/stable debut; this one, bought for 190,000euros after two wins in France (on soft and AW), fits the bill with a tongue-tie added; has won over 1m7f, and never raced over less than 1m4f, but likely she's shown enough pace at home to come here.

4.32.betting_forecast: 7/2 Copper Craft, 9/2 She's Ideal, 11/2 Sarangpur, 6/1 Cleopatra's Needle, 9/1 Giselles Defence, 12/1 Cuckaloo Hill, Keilah, 14/1
4.32.spotlight_verdict: Copper Craft holds strong claims following a good recent AW effort over this trip, while She's Ideal is another with a strong chance if staying this longer trip. However, the vote goes to SARANGPUR, who shaped really well on handicap debut at Gowran and could appreciate this better ground. Cleopatra's Needle is another to consider, and one to keep an eye on in the market is the top-weight Giselles Defence. [Alan Hewison]

horses.spotlight_comment: Maiden runs over various trips haven't amounted to much and ran no sort of race upped to 1m4f for handicap debut when last seen in September; hard to make a case for.

Sole Flat win (from 30 starts) in 1m2f Navan handicap in 2024; better hurdler, winning at last year's Galway festival and ran a cracker on return to finish second in 1m Leopardstown Flat handicap last month; race may have come too soon when never counting over hurdles six days later, but has to be respected back on the level.
Low-grade handicapper but in good form on the AW of late, most recently 13-8 fav when only denied second late on over this trip 10 days ago; same mark here, should go well.
horses.breeding: ch g Raven's Pass - Mise En Rose

horses.spotlight_comment: Won four times for Ian Williams on a variety of ground, all at 1m2f; nothing for this yard at big odds until mildly encouraging run at Bellewstown last time; drops in class now and has his ground, worth a market check.
horses.breeding: b g National Defense - Cotton Camera

horses.spotlight_comment: Won over 7f when trained in Poland; showed a glimmer at Dundalk in January (over this trip) but didn't back it up back there later that month and off since; 2lb wrong here.
horses.breeding: b g Sioux Nation - Beyond Dance

horses.spotlight_comment: Sole win for Willie McCreery came over 1m1f at Punchestown in 2024; some decent efforts in defeat last season and picked up for 5,000euros in November; debuts for local yard in first-time tongue-tie and market could be interesting.

Career-best over just shy of this trip on handicap debut at Gowran last month when up with much of pace in finishing third on soft ground; quicker ground and sharper track could enable him to see this out, so definite player.
Comeback run at Gowran last month was promising (staying-on fourth over 1m); first attempt at this longer trip, but handicapped to go well if she stays.
horses.breeding: br f Belardo - Vocal Warm Up

horses.spotlight_comment: Very lightly-raced 4yo filly enters handicaps after three maiden runs over much shorter trips; potential improver, market may guide.
Maiden showed bits and pieces of form last year at 1m whne with Johnny Murtagh; , soft ground at Gowran latest probably wasn't ideal, others preferred though.

5.07.betting_forecast: 100/30 Down The Glen, 9/2 Augusta Rock, 6/1 Misty Cove, 7/1 Nephin Mountain, Sands Castle, 9/1 Kart Of Gold, 10/1 Pliny,
5.07.spotlight_verdict: Michael Mulvany won this two years ago and had the runner-up last year, so a chance is taken that NEPHIN MOUNTAIN, a staying-on fourth over 7f last time, improves for stepping up to this trip. Down The Glen should stay and shaped well on his return, but may prefer softer ground. Joseph O'Brien has a formidable record in this type of race and the well-bred Augusta Rock could easily contend, while Sands Castle is well treated on paper after an improved run in a maiden. Kart Of Gold is not ruled out with a good claimer booked. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Beaten 4l on handicap debut over 1m at Dundalk in November; hampered early on when not as good back there the following month; bred to get this trip.

Homebred nursery winner over 7f on heavy ground and staying-on sixth over 1m (soft) in higher-grade Curragh contest on recent return to action; dam won over 1m and he should stay, but easy ground is said to be important to him.
Half-sister to five winners from 7f to 1m6f, several of them useful; huge prices when out the back in AW maidens; tried in a hood last time, now goes with cheekpieces; 3lb wrong.
horses.breeding: b f Space Blues - Music And Dance

horses.spotlight_comment: Two good runs in 7f handicaps at Gowran and stayed on steadily last time when beaten 7l by well-handicapped winner; sire not really an influence for stamina, but he might improve for this longer trip, and yard has good record in the race.

Placed twice over 7f, including when second in AW claimer in March, but most exposed of these and not sure what trip he wants; well held over this distance and 1m4f last twice; down 16lb from initial rating.
Much-improved fourth at huge price in 1m maiden at Gowran, staying on steadily to finish only 2l off 83-rated third; well handicapped in theory on that line of form.
horses.breeding: b f Sands Of Mali - Light At Dawn

horses.spotlight_comment: Cheap yearling ran okay at Galway on sole start at two; quiet in two Curragh maidens this term; very stoutly bred.
horses.breeding: ch g Decorated Knight - Dazzling Light

horses.spotlight_comment: Ran okay in 7f/1m maidens last year; long layoff and not really bred to appreciate this longer trip; small yard amongst the winners lately.
